judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate claims-made caption whose terms ('claims-made and reported', 'discovered and reported') are all defined or elaborated elsewhere; nothing in it is genuinely two-sided on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states claims are covered only if reported 'during the policy period', while Insuring Agreements I.A/I.B (c008/c009) and Section VIII (c076) permit reporting during an 'extended reporting period', a mismatch a court could be asked to harmonise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short integration listing of the documents making up the policy; its terms are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives no order of precedence among the form, the Declarations and the sixteen endorsements, several of which (Endorsements 5, 8, 10, 11) purport to delete and replace the same provisions, so the reach of this clause could matter.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '100 % minimum-earned as of the first day of the Policy Period ... whichever is earlier' is awkward and the OCR is garbled, but the intent (fully earned premium) is discernible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely conflicts with General Condition IX.A.3 (c079), which contemplates remaining 'unearned premium' earned pro rata and refunded within thirty days of cancellation — impossible if 100% is minimum-earned at inception.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical all-caps notice repeated in the policy form; the wording is standard and self-explanatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same tension as c001 with the extended reporting period provisions (c076, c129) which allow post-period reporting of claims deemed made on the last day of the policy period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional signpost saying quoted terms are defined in Section V; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several endorsements add quoted terms ('transportation', 'covered operations', 'non-owned covered locations') and 'covered operations' in Endorsement 6 is never defined anywhere, which slightly undercuts this promise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration and reliance recital; the language is conventional and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces the Representations condition (c084) and the Fraud exclusion (c059) rather than contradicting anything.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lead-in conditioning coverage on the Declarations identifying the coverage as underwritten; plain in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations Items 2 and 3 do identify Coverages A and B, and supplemental coverages are added by endorsement, so the lead-in fits, subject only to whether endorsement-added coverages are 'identified on the Declarations'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'first commence, in their entirety, during the policy period' is a demanding and contestable temporal test, and 'arising out of a pollution condition' carries the usual breadth questions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 5 (c120) and Endorsement 10 (c136) each purport to delete this same Subsection A 'in its entirety' and replace it with different text, leaving genuine doubt as to which version governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'commenced, in whole or part, prior to the policy period' is workable, though the OCR typo 'nolicy period' and the whole/part split invite argument about conditions straddling inception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Coverage A (c008), which requires commencement 'in their entirety' during the period, the two together are designed to be complementary but leave the boundary case to be argued; the Divested Property exclusion (c055) expressly carves Coverage B out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and internally consistent attachment mechanics for the self-insured retention; the obligations are stated twice over for clarity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4 (c108) sets a separate Catastrophe Management-Specific retention and Endorsement 6 alters what erodes limits, but neither contradicts this attachment rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A per-condition limit tied to a Declarations item; definite and arithmetic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.I (c121) deletes and replaces this exact subsection, so the original text has been superseded and its continued presence is at most a housekeeping artefact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain aggregate limit cross-referring to Item 2.c.; nothing to construe in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Superseded by Endorsement 6.I.D (c122), and the Item 2.c. figure ($9,000,000) exceeds the Total Policy Aggregate in Item 4 ($7,000,000), a numerical mismatch the 'subject to' language must absorb.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mirror-image per-condition limit for Coverage B; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deleted and replaced by Endorsement 6.I.E (c123), which adds an undefined qualifier ('resulting from covered operations') absent here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mirror-image aggregate limit for Coverage B; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deleted and replaced by Endorsement 6.I.F (c124), again with the undefined 'covered operations' qualifier, so which text controls is not free from doubt.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A total-aggregate cap expressed clearly and made 'subject to' the coverage-specific limits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 4's $7,000,000 total is smaller than Coverage A's $9,000,000 aggregate in Item 2.c. (c012), so the Declarations and this subsection sit uneasily together even if the cap is meant to control.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'continuous, repeated, or related pollution condition' is an undefined and elastic relatedness test, and 'no other policy shall respond' is a strong deeming provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with the single-retention sentence in II.A (c010) and the per-condition limits (c011/c013) without contradicting them, though its reach across prior ACE policies is outside this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard duty-to-defend clause with clearly stated end-points; the 'to which this insurance applies' formula is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.II (c125) deletes and replaces this subsection with a three-limb exhaustion test keyed to the dedicated defence sublimit, so the original is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully drafted counsel-selection clause; 'reasonable proximity' and 'similar complexity' are soft but the structure is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.IV.F (c128) gives the first named insured the right to select counsel after exhaustion of the defence sublimit, a regime that must be read together with, not against, this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Saying the insured has 'the right and the duty' to retain a consultant while also requiring the insurer's prior written consent is a mild internal pull, though the practical meaning is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4.III (c110) deletes and replaces this very subsection to add catastrophe management firms, so the original text no longer operates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence stating defence costs erode limits and apply to the retention; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deleted and replaced by Endorsement 6.II.D (c126), which substitutes the dedicated defence sublimit, so the two texts describe different erosion mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'does not impose any additional unreasonable burdens' is soft, but the consequence of refusing a recommended settlement is spelled out precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.IV.F (c128) restates a garbled version of the same hammer clause for post-exhaustion claims, creating two overlapping settlement regimes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'pollution conditions located ... within the United States' is short and could be tested where a condition migrates across a border, but the intent is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the definition of 'non-owned disposal site' as amended (c133), which is likewise limited to sites within the United States.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines additional insureds by reference to endorsement and limits their rights to those specified; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 2 (c093) names Hoffman Rettig and confines it to vicarious liability, exactly as this definition contemplates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but standard bodily injury definition; 'prospective medical monitoring costs' is delimited by its own purpose clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds the Employers Liability exclusion (c056) and the claim definition (c026) without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A technical credential definition requiring mutual agreement; the qualifications language is detailed rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 (c144) excludes all fungi and legionella claims and costs, leaving this definition and the fungi limb of 'remediation costs' (c047) with little or nothing to operate on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'written assertion of a legal right ... including, but not limited to' is an open catch-all with enumerated specifics, the classic setting for a scope argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This definition is deleted and replaced twice, by Endorsement 8.II (c132) and Endorsement 11.II (c141), each for a different purpose, so which text applies to a given claim needs working out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise definition of third-party carriage with a defined end point (unloading); little room for two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 10.II (c137) deletes Subsection E entirely and substitutes 'transportation', so 'contingent transportation' no longer exists even though exclusion Q in the base form (c069) still refers to it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-limb definition dependent on schedules; the numbering is garbled but the content is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both Endorsement 8.I (c131) and Endorsement 11.I (c140) purport to delete and replace this same Subsection F with materially different versions, and Endorsement 11's version refers to a Schedule of Non-Owned Disposal Sites that is not attached.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A hard seventy-two hour window plus an 'imminent and substantial threat' standard; the latter is a familiar regulatory phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It functions as the consent carve-out in III.C (c019/c110) and VII.C (c073/c117) consistently across those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tightly drawn: the obligation must be 'explicitly included' in a contract listed on a schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Schedule of Insured Contracts Endorsement is attached to this policy, so the carve-back to the Contractual Liability exclusion (c054) is empty in practice — a coherence point a court could be asked about.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'guidance document' and 'rule' inside a sweeping definition of environmental law give the term unusually elastic edges for a gateway definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It controls the reach of 'remediation costs' (c047) and 'government action' (c035); those provisions depend on it but do not contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining the ERP as time to report a claim 'first made against the insured during or subsequent to the end of the policy period' is odd for a claims-made policy that elsewhere requires the claim to be first made during the period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Insuring Agreements A and B (c008/c009), which require the claim to be first made during the policy period, and against VIII.B (c076), which says the ERP does not change the scope of coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assigns premium, retention and agency functions to one identified entity; clear and complete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Dovetails with 'named insured' (c041), the retention attachment rule (c010) and the ERP conditions (c078/c130) without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but self-referential definition ('byproducts produced or released by fungi'); the circularity is minor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 (c143/c144) removes fungi from 'pollution condition' and excludes fungi claims outright, so this definition survives with no operative field.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward: agency action taken under authority of 'environmental law'; the elasticity comes from the incorporated definition, not this one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the 'claim' definition (c026), which lists government action as an included form of claim.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of irritants closing with 'or waste materials' and 'medical, infectious and pathological wastes' invites an ejusdem generis argument about the catch-all's reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is incorporated into 'pollution condition' both in the base form (c045) and as amended by Endorsement 12 (c143), which is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition uses 'insured' within its own definition of 'insured' ('employee of ... any insured'), a small circularity, and the trailing scope-of-duties qualifier could be read to attach to more than one antecedent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the Insured vs. Insured exclusion (c061) and Separation of Insureds (c085), which speaks only of 'named insureds' though the policy applies to a wider class of 'insureds'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonable legal costs, charges, and expenses, including expert charges' is standard; 'reasonable' is a familiar judicial standard rather than an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the erosion provisions (c020, c126) and the dedicated defence sublimit (c127).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A technical waste classification tracking federal categories; 'greater than specified quantities' leaves the specification unstated but the category is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only inside 'illicit abandonment' (c036) and 'pollution condition' (c045/c143); no tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by reference to two named federal statutes as amended; about as determinate as a definition gets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with the same 'pollution condition' and 'illicit abandonment' provisions without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear cross-reference giving named insureds the same rights except those reserved to the first named insured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Subsection K (c033) and with the Separation of Insureds condition (c085), which likewise operates only at the 'named insured' level.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long statutory-style definition; 'other such resources' is a catch-all but is anchored by the preceding enumeration and the trusteeship requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12.III (c145) imposes a $500,000 sublimit on natural resource damage claims, which supplements rather than contradicts this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, broad definition ('any disposal site or recycling facility not owned or operated by an insured') with no qualifiers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 8.II (c133) deletes and replaces this definition with a far narrower, condition-laden version, so the base text is superseded and the two cannot both operate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb 2 is syntactically broken ('the period of time following the closing date ... or, as applicable, through the applicable expiration date'), leaving the start and end of the period for acquired locations unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Automatic Acquisition endorsement is attached, so limb 2 has no field of operation here; limb 1 matches Declarations Items 2.a and 3.a.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant, contaminant, or pollutant' followed by an illustrative list is the archetypal pollution-definition dispute, and whether a biological agent counts is genuinely contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated limbs including 'diminished value' and 'loss of use'; broad but each limb is defined and bounded to third-party property.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'to the extent required by environmental law' is the operative constraint and is highly contestable in application, as is 'reasonable expenses'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any employee ... responsible for environmental affairs, control, or compliance' has soft edges but is anchored by the officer/director limb.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to Declarations Items 2.d and 3.d, plus endorsement variation; definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long structured definition of terrorism whose limbs ('to further political, ideological ... objectives') are broad but are standard industry language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the War or Terrorism exclusion (c070); no other provision qualifies it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A quantified definition (more than ten percent of volume below ground) with express exclusions for septic tanks and separators; unusually precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the UST exclusion (c068), which applies it consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sweeping list ending in 'any use of military force, usurped power or confiscation ... by any government, military or other authority', which could be argued to reach ordinary governmental action.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'arising out of or related to asbestos' is broad, and the carve-back turns on the fine distinction of asbestos 'discovered in soil or groundwater'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel in form to the Lead-Based Paint exclusion (c064) and consistent with the remediation-costs definition (c047).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'except if the liability would have attached in the absence of such contract' proviso is standard but perennially argued.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its carve-back for 'environmental indemnity obligations' (c030) depends on a Schedule of Insured Contracts Endorsement that is not attached to this policy, leaving the exception with nothing to operate on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear on its terms: conditions first commencing after the location was sold, abandoned, given away or condemned.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The sentence 'This exclusion shall not apply to Coverage B' is close to self-cancelling, since Coverage B (c009) covers only conditions commencing before the policy period while the exclusion addresses conditions commencing after divestiture.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional employers-liability exclusion; the misnumbered '4.' is plainly an OCR artefact rather than a meaning-changing error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the 'insured' (c037) and 'bodily injury' (c024) definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any associated claims seeking exclusively injunctive relief in addition to such fines' is syntactically confused, and the punitive-damages carve-back reverses much of the exclusion's opening words.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion is broad ('or otherwise in the care, custody, or control') but its carve-back for remediation costs is explicit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and clear about who must have committed the fraud and when; materiality is a familiar standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Cancellation 2.b (c079/c135) and is expressly carved out of Separation of Insureds (c085), which is coherent though it makes one insured's fraud bite others.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excluding all in-house costs, then restoring anything approved by the insurer 'at its sole discretion', gives the insurer an unbounded gatekeeping power that a court could be asked to constrain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence with no qualification; because 'insured' (c037) sweeps in employees, officers and additional insureds, the exclusion's literal reach is startlingly wide.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Separation of Insureds (c085) expressly disapplies itself to this exclusion, so the wide reading is reinforced rather than cured, which is itself a point of tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'intentional disregard of, or knowing, willful, or deliberate non-compliance with' any law or 'instruction of any governmental agency' is broad and state-of-mind dependent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Keyed to 'responsible person' (c048) and excepted from Separation of Insureds (c085), consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in existence and reported to a responsible person' is a compound trigger whose components (existence, reporting, knowledge) could be read several ways, and the exception numbering is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both carve-backs depend on a Schedule of Known Conditions Endorsement that is not attached, and the UST exclusion (c068) cross-refers to that same absent schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short exclusion with a soil/groundwater carve-back mirroring the asbestos exclusion; clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c053 and with 'remediation costs' (c047).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'materially increases the likelihood or severity of a pollution condition' measured against 'intended uses or operations identified' in the application is an inherently contestable comparison.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on application materials outside the four corners, and is excepted from Separation of Insureds (c085); no direct clash with another operative provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'naturally occurring materials' and the carve-back for substances present 'as a result of human activities or human processes' are both undefined and their boundary is genuinely uncertain, especially in an agricultural setting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the 'pollution condition' definitions (c045/c143), it is unclear whether biological or animal-derived matter is excluded as natural or covered as human-caused.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean exclusion with a schedule-based carve-back; the words are plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 8.III (c134) deletes and replaces this exclusion entirely with a differently structured 'Disposal Sites' exclusion, so the base text is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The connectors are broken: the knowledge condition ends 'and' before two limbs joined by 'or', so whether both or either limb must be satisfied is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both limbs cross-refer to schedules (Insured USTs; Known Conditions) that are not attached to this policy, so the exclusion's exceptions are inoperative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion itself is clear; the conditional carve-back ('if such coverage is added ... by endorsement') simply points elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 10.III (c138) deletes and replaces this exclusion, and Endorsement 10.II (c137) replaces 'contingent transportation' with 'transportation', so this text and its defined term no longer cohere with the policy as issued.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'attributable, whether directly or indirectly' and the anti-concurrent-causation tail are broad but are settled industry formulations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the 'war' (c052) and 'terrorism' (c050) definitions and is consistent with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause mixes mandatory and permissive language — notice 'must' be given as soon as practicable but 'should include' the listed details — and 'as soon as practicable' is itself a classic litigated standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the Declarations caption (c001/c004) and the insuring agreements (c008/c009), which require written reporting within the policy period, a stricter trigger than 'as soon as practicable'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of cooperation duties, garbled in numbering but each duty is clear; 'reasonably require' is a familiar limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Legal Action condition (c081), which conditions suit on full compliance with policy terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A firm voluntary-payment/consent bar with a single emergency-response exception; plain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'make every attempt to mitigate any loss' is an unusually open obligation, and the insurer's right to act 'in the sole judgment of the insurer' is unconstrained on its face.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three clear sentences with an express deeming rule; little to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite sentence granting a sixty-day free reporting tail.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and conditional but definite; the 'not more than two hundred percent' cap and the request deadline are precise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Paragraph 3 is confusingly drafted — it calls the Item 5 'premium percentage' the minimum-earned premium and then speaks of remaining unearned premium earned pro rata — so the refund entitlement is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive inspection right with a disclaimer of any undertaking; conventional and clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stands alongside the Service of Suit endorsement (c152) and the New York jurisdiction clause (c087), which together create a contested picture of where and when the insurer can be sued.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence assumes underlying insurance and excess/drop-down mechanics that do not match a policy written with a self-insured retention rather than underlying limits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That sentence sits oddly with Other Insurance (c086) and the retention-attachment provision (c010), which make this a primary policy above an SIR, not an excess policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The priority waterfall is stated in order and the expense-sharing formula is arithmetic; the second 'then to the insured' repetition is minor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Converting application statements into 'warranties' is a consequential characterisation but is stated in three unambiguous numbered points.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long list of carve-outs preceding the operative rule, and the rule speaks only of 'named insureds' although the policy elsewhere protects a broader class of 'insureds'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard excess-of-other-insurance wording; 'other valid and collectible insurance' is a familiar and workable phrase.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An ordinary and comprehensive choice-of-law clause naming a single state's law; nothing internally ambiguous.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional no-waiver, no-oral-modification and anti-assignment clause; clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence headings clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Harmless, though the policy relies heavily on headings ('NEW POLLUTION CONDITIONS', exclusion captions) when endorsements identify the text they replace.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, standard reasonableness overlay on consents; its own words are clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line schedule adding a single named insured; purely mechanical.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Actual business interruption loss ... in excess of the Deductible Period' mixes a time-based deductible with a monetary excess formula, and the reporting trigger combines 'as soon as practicable' with 'during the policy period'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Net profit or loss, before income taxes ... that would have been realized' is a counterfactual measure open to argument, though it is standard business-income language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 'business interruption' (c096) and the period-of-interruption rules (c104/c105); no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'necessary partial or complete suspension' turns on the undefined word 'necessary', which is the usual battleground in business-interruption claims.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 'period of interruption' (c101) and 'suspension' (c103), although the latter is defined only for rented locations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-item composite definition; the missing closing quotation mark on 'Extra expense' does not change meaning.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is convoluted — coverage exists only 'for remediation costs resulting from the first-party discovery' of the condition — and the phrase 'first-party discovery' is not defined anywhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It narrows business interruption cover by reference to Coverages A and B (c008/c009) and to the exclusions, and its interaction with the amended 'pollution condition' definition (c143) determines whether any given loss qualifies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Restricted to 'a covered location under development' with a closed list of five expense heads; the opening syntax is clumsy but the list is exhaustive.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires costs both 'necessary to avoid or mitigate' interruption and incurred 'to actually minimize' foregone income, a double standard that could be applied strictly or loosely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the mitigation duty in VII.D (c074) and with the Insured's Internal Expenses exclusion (c060), but does not contradict them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition fixes only the commencement of the period and says nothing about its end, and 'necessarily suspended' repeats the undefined necessity standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The missing end point is supplied by Condition IV.B (c105) and the start rule by IV.A (c104), so the gap is filled elsewhere in the same endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short measure of actual lost rental fees; the only softness is the OCR'd word 'fost' for 'lost'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on 'suspension' (c103) and feeds 'business income' (c095) coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'untenantable for the purposes identified to the Insurer at the inception of the Policy' points outside the document to unidentified communications, making the standard hard to apply from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is confined to rented covered locations while 'business interruption' (c096) covers the insured's own operations, a scope mismatch within the same endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Slightly circular ('if such business interruption delays the start of the insured's operations'), but the counterfactual start date rule is understandable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence denies coverage for loss of business income caused by 'unfavorable business conditions caused by the impact of the covered pollution condition' — a phrase that could swallow much of the coverage and is genuinely open to competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That carve-out pulls against the Supplemental Coverage grant in c094 and the 'business income' definition (c095), which measure exactly the income the condition prevented.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional appraisal mechanism, but it says the appraisers' decision is 'binding upon both parties' while also preserving the insurer's right to deny the claim, which cuts against finality.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reference to 'a judge of a court having jurisdiction' interacts with the New York exclusive-jurisdiction clause (c087) and the Service of Suit endorsement (c152), and the reservation of denial rights sits against the binding-decision sentence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any of the individually excluded exposures identified above' has no clear antecedent in the endorsement, so which exclusions are imported is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It purports to add to Section VI (miscited as 'VIL') and must borrow content from the policy's exclusions (c053–c070) and from the 'covered pollution condition' definition (c098) to have meaning.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two dollar figures with labels; purely numerical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The catastrophe-specific retention sits alongside the general 'self-insured retention' definition (c049) and the coverage grant in c109, which refers simply to 'the self-insured retention', leaving a small question of which applies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in excess of the self-insured retention' does not say which retention, and 'catastrophe management events that first commence, in their entirety' repeats an awkward temporal test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to the general retention while the same endorsement (c108) sets a specific one, and the sublimit is made subject to the Declarations limits, where the Total Policy Aggregate is $7,000,000.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Like the provision it replaces, it gives the insured 'the right and the duty' to retain a firm while requiring the insurer's prior written consent, a mild internal pull.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonably likely to have a negative impact on the insured with respect to its income, reputation, community relations, public confidence or good will' is an open-ended standard with no measurable boundary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger rests on 'the good faith opinion of a key executive', a subjective standard, and requires two conditions joined by 'and' after a colon that is easy to misread.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It builds on 'pollution condition' (as amended by c143) and 'adverse media coverage' (c111) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined purely by insurer written approval; determinate though one-sided.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'minimizing potential harm ... by managing adverse media coverage and maintaining and restoring public confidence' describes a service in impressionistic terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list ends with 'or other necessary response costs' after a series of specific heads, a textbook ejusdem generis catch-all, and item 2 is garbled ('mailing of materials of public relations materials').

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of named offices plus an approval mechanism for additional titles; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the catastrophe event trigger (c112) and does not overlap awkwardly with 'responsible person' (c048).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule with several plainly mistyped retroactive dates ('11/01/2074', '11/07/2014') and OCR-mangled column headings, and coverage designations that differ location by location.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain aggregate-limit statement keyed to Item 2.c.; nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three clearly enumerated end-points for the duty to defend; well structured.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence stating a double erosion (defence sublimit and Item 4 aggregate) plus application to the retention; clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dollar sublimit with an express subordination to the Item 4 aggregate; unambiguous.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The settlement sentence is broken on its face — 'If the insurer recommends a settlement of any ongoing or future claim for which it is not which is acceptable to a claimant' — and it uses the undefined term 'loss'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One conditional sentence granting a ninety-day tail; definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed conditions with precise numbers; the only oddity is requiring the request before policy expiry when the entitlement may arise on cancellation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision as printed is scrambled, with the heading fragment 'H. Solely with respect to coverage ...' embedded in the middle of the definition, and its limb 3 cross-refers to 'Subsection D., above' which appears later.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four cumulative conditions followed by 'or' limb 2; the conditions are objective but the 'or' placement after subparagraph (d) makes the structure hard to parse.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement grant is workmanlike; 'resulting from transportation' is defined in the same endorsement (c137).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise definition with a stated end point (unloading); the only slack is 'other conveyance'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard vehicle-pollution exclusion with a one-line carve-back; clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The schedule is badly scrambled in the document — a bare column of numbers 1 to 11 detached from eleven site names — so which entries are actually listed is a matter of reconstruction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The core phrase 'any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant, contaminant, or pollutant' followed by an illustrative list is the classic pollution-definition battleground, and the added sentence that the term 'does not include any odor' invites argument about what else is excluded by implication.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes the whole subject matter of c025, c034 and part of c047, and it duplicates the odour carve-out already made in the replaced pollution definition (c143).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sublimit sentence with an express subordination to the Declarations limits; arithmetic and clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three figures and a retroactive date in schedule form; nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'arises out of the use of a product ... after the insured has relinquished possession' and the sentence 'products do not include waste products' are both capable of narrow and broad readings.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short sanctions clause; it switches to 'us' where the rest of the policy says 'the Insurer', but the meaning is not in doubt.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the company will submit to the jurisdiction of any court of competent jurisdiction' at the insured's request is broad and unqualified, and whether it confers a right on the insured or merely waives objections to service is genuinely arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'other than as above stated' is the pivot: it preserves the policy terms except to the extent the endorsement says otherwise, and how far the endorsement 'states otherwise' about forum is precisely what is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the provision that must mediate between the Service of Suit submission (c152) and the exclusive New York jurisdiction clause (c087), and it is capable of being read either to preserve or to displace that clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A signature-attribution statement plus an acknowledgement of validity; nothing operative to construe.
